title: Global Verdier duality
statement:
Fix primes $p$ and $\ell$ with $\ell\ne p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$ with $q$ elements, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on finite-type $k$-schemes at these coefficient stages, with its axioms (A1)--(A6) and their specified constructible finite-Tor domains. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and fix $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite
type and geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of pure dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] over $k$, with
structure morphism $a_X$. Use the constructible exceptional inverse image
$Ra_X^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], at the coefficient stage
specified above. At every finite stage $A_{E,m}$, $m\geq1$, the structure
morphism is exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility], with cohomological and Tor bounds independent of
$m$, since it is separated of finite type. At integral and field stages
use the integral, rationalized, and common-stage exceptional functors in
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the adjunctions specified by the
fixed datum [def-sf-datum]. No additional admissibility hypothesis is imposed. Assume either
that $X$ is proper, or that $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated
finite-type, geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$; in the latter
case no properness is required. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Then
there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma\bigl(X,\mathbb D_XK\bigr)
$$

in the point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], natural in $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$
and compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, and shifts. For
$K=\Lambda_X$ it specializes to
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda)^\vee\cong R\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$.

Here $\mathbb D_XK$ and $\omega_X$ have the meanings of [def-sf-pf], and
$R\Gamma_c,R\Gamma$ are the coefficient complexes of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The displayed isomorphism is first
an isomorphism in the coefficient-complex target of $\operatorname{Fib}_s$
of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]: $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$,
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, or the stagewise
$D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, according to $\Lambda$.
Its formulation in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ means its transport through the
inverse of that equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]. The superscript $\vee$ in the coefficient
category means $R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$, at a common finite
field stage for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Finite-reduction compatibility
is asserted at finite and integral coefficients, and rationalization and
scalar-extension compatibility at the field stages where those operations
are defined, as in axiom (A5) of [def-sf-datum].

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $C_K=Ra_{X!}K$, and $B_K=Ra_{X*}\mathbb D_XK$. The structure morphism $a_X$ is separated of finite type by the hypotheses, and its target $s$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. The current statement of [def-trf-admissibility] therefore supplies its constructible exceptional adjunction at every finite stage, with cohomological and Tor bounds independent of the quotient exponent. This citation concerns finite coefficients only; at integral and field stages the adjunction and its coefficient comparisons are the specified clauses (A1) and (A5) of [def-sf-datum]. The finite-stage admissibility definition's composition conjugate and exchange $Rg'_*Rf'^!\cong Rf^!Rg_*$ are not needed in this specialization. Axiom (A6) of [def-sf-datum] puts $\mathbb D_XK$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, so all the functors in this expression are applied on their stipulated domains. In particular, both source $X$ and target $s$ satisfy the separated-scheme hypothesis in the current statement of [thm-sf-verdier-exchange]. Axiom (A1) of the datum also puts $C_K=Ra_{X!}K$ in $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, and (A6) puts $D_sC_K$ there, as needed for the point tensor comparisons below. The hypotheses of [thm-sf-verdier-exchange] hold with $f=a_X$, $Y=s$, and $M=K$; it gives its specified canonical natural isomorphism $e_K:D_s C_K\xrightarrow{\sim}B_K$, including its coefficient and shift compatibilities. This is the exchange step of the unit, not a separate global-duality theorem being assumed.

source.place: Paragraph 1, first sentence: specialize Verdier exchange to the structure morphism

proof.text: Let $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$. Use the four separate exact equivalences of [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], with targets as stated there; no higher coefficient stage is identified with $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$. By [lem-sf-point], $\omega_s\cong\Lambda_s$, and its internal-Hom identification gives $\alpha_K:F(D_s C_K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(F C_K,\Lambda)$. Use only these point-dualizing and internal-Hom assertions of that lemma, not its incorrectly uniform finite-ring target. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], $F C_K=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and $F B_K=R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$. Define the displayed arrow to be $g_K=F(e_K)\circ\alpha_K^{-1}$. Both factors are isomorphisms, so $g_K$ is an isomorphism in the appropriate coefficient category. Applying an inverse of the equivalence $F$ expresses the same arrow in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, precisely the point-category interpretation in the statement.

source.place: Paragraph 1, evaluation and point identifications; corrected four-stage typing

proof.text: The comparison $\alpha_K$ is the internal-Hom comparison under the monoidal point equivalence, not an arbitrary objectwise isomorphism. Indeed [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] gives its natural tensor and unit comparisons, and [lem-sf-point] identifies the dualizing object at the point with the unit. The comparison on duals is characterized by carrying evaluation $C_K\otimes^L D_s C_K\to\Lambda_s$ to coefficient evaluation: composing $F$ of this evaluation with the inverse tensor comparison yields $F C_K\otimes^L F(D_s C_K)\to\Lambda$, whose tensor-Hom transpose is $\alpha_K$. Uniqueness of a transpose proves naturality. Explicitly, for $u:K\to K'$, put $c=Ra_{X!}u:C_K\to C_{K'}$ and $h_B=Ra_{X*}(\mathbb D_Xu):B_{K'}\to B_K$. Naturality says $e_K\circ D_s(c)=h_B\circ e_{K'}$ and $\alpha_K\circ F(D_s(c))=(F(c))^\vee\circ\alpha_{K'}$. Multiplying these equations by the appropriate inverses of $\alpha$ gives $g_K\circ(F(c))^\vee=F(h_B)\circ g_{K'}$. Thus the arrow is canonical and contravariantly natural in $K$, as required.

source.place: Paragraph 1, naturality of the composite: explicit evaluation characterization

proof.text: For an allowed coefficient change $S$, let $b_L:S(F C_K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}(F C_{SK})^\vee$ and $b_R:S(F B_K)\xrightarrow{\sim}F B_{SK}$ denote the comparisons furnished by the datum, the exchange theorem, and the point identifications. The point tensor and unit comparisons of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] commute with finite reduction and scalar extension. The integral point reduction is the actual canonical sections comparison of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction]; the integral/rational scalar comparison and its identity/tower equations are [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Consequently the two paths comparing $\alpha$ before and after $S$ have the same tensor-Hom transpose: both are $S$ of evaluation followed by the coefficient-unit comparison, using the tensor associator. They therefore agree. Combine this equality with the coefficient-compatibility square for $e_K$ in [thm-sf-verdier-exchange]. Substituting $g_K=F(e_K)\alpha_K^{-1}$ and cancelling the adjacent comparison and inverse yields the required square $b_R\circ S(g_K)=g_{SK}\circ b_L$. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ form the square over a common finite field and take its morphism class; the identity/tower equations for the point scalar comparison identify it with the same square over every larger common field. Finite reduction is used only at the stages covered by (A5) of [def-sf-datum]; there is no reduction functor from a rational field to $A_{E,n}$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, coefficient compatibilities of the two ingredients, with comparison square written out

proof.text: For an integer $r$, duality has $D_X(K[r])=D_X(K)[-r]$ and $D_s(C[r])=D_s(C)[-r]$, under the usual Hom-complex shift identifications. The exchange isomorphism respects these shift identifications by [thm-sf-verdier-exchange], and the evaluation functor commutes with shifts by [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]. The comparison $\alpha$ uses the same evaluation and Hom shift convention: the evaluation for a shifted first argument and oppositely shifted dual is the shifted evaluation, with its standard Hom-complex sign. Thus substituting into the formula for $g$ gives $g_{K[r]}=g_K[-r]$ under the canonical source and target identifications. This is the asserted shift compatibility.

Finally take $K=\Lambda_X$. By [def-sf-pf], $\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X=R\mathcal H om_X(\Lambda_X,\omega_X)$ with $\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda_s$. Evaluation at $1$ identifies this internal Hom with $\omega_X$. To see the identity directly from [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], take its K-injective representative $I$ of $\omega_X$: the Hom complex from the coefficient unit concentrated in degree zero has in degree $j$ precisely $\mathcal H om(\Lambda_X,I^j)=I^j$, by $\phi\mapsto\phi(1)$, and differential the differential of $I$. Its inverse sends $v$ to $(a\mapsto av)$. These are natural inverse chain maps. The integral unit is the completed coefficient sheaf, so the identical module calculation applies there; rationalization and common-stage scalar extension apply these same maps. Substitution into $g_{\Lambda_X}$ proves the constant-coefficient clause. All preceding applications require only that $a_X$ be separated of finite type. Those hypotheses hold in both cases in the statement; none of the steps equates $Ra_{X!}$ with $Ra_{X*}$, so the descent case is covered even when $X$ is nonproper.

theorem global_verdier_duality (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [GeometricallyConnected (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (d : ℕ) (_hd : X.IsPureDimension d)
    (_hX : GeometricAlternative D (Over.mk (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k)))) :
    Assertion l Ω D hl X
lean.note: Exact existing four-stage global Verdier duality, already recorded by sk-thm-sf-global-duality. The current blueprint unit and this expanded node assert the same canonical natural isomorphism, coefficient and signed-shift squares, and same-component constant specialization. The theorem universally quantifies over the published normalized constructible exceptional systems; these are the actual operations fixed by the six-functor datum, so it applies in that datum without an extra admissibility assumption. Package and its Conclusion use the literal identity operation at the point, actual internal Hom and projection/evaluation components, and all four coefficient stages. The coefficient-complex formulation is its transport under the recorded four point-fibre equivalences. No second declaration or module is written.
